records.title: Cuidado con el Ángel
records.meta: Telenovela · Mexico (Televisa, Las Estrellas 2008–09) · Spanish · Brazil: SBT 'Cuidado com o Anjo' (2022 rerun)
records.summary: Psychoanalyst João Miguel suspects his wife Viviana is faking amnesia. He tells Eduardo he will hypnotize her, then does so without her noticing. Under hypnosis she confesses she never lost her memory, faked her own death, and reveals everything she did while away; afterwards she denies all of it. In a later episode he puts the counsellor Branca under hypnosis therapy to investigate her past.
records.method: Covert hypnosis to extract a confession
records.pregnancy_note: Viviana is not pregnant; the pregnant character is Malú (by João Miguel).

episodes.gist: João Miguel decides to hypnotize Viviana and begins.
Hypnotized Viviana confesses she never had amnesia and faked her death; she later denies it.
João Miguel uses hypnosis therapy on Branca to explore her childhood (dissociative identity diagnosis).

records.title: Wife Was Hypnotized By Husband, Became Slave To Mistress, But He Didn't Know That She Was Pretending!
records.meta: Short drama (full compilation) · China (English dub/subtitles) · YouTube: Sweet Hearth Drama · uploaded 13 Aug 2025 · runtime about 65 min
records.character: The wife ('Miss Pei', addressed as 'Judge'); her husband; his 'cousin' (the mistress)
records.summary: A husband and his mistress, whom he passes off as his 'cousin', try to hypnotize his wealthy wife ('Look into my eyes… you're feeling very sleepy'), make her kneel and sign papers, and keep her as their servant. The hypnosis has stopped working, and she pretends to be under while gathering proof. The mistress turns up pregnant with the husband's child. The wife records his confession that he cut the brakes that killed her parents and takes him down at the shareholders' meeting.
records.pregnant_end_note: The mistress, not the wife, is pregnant ('I still have your child in my belly').

episodes.gist: Failed induction: 'How could the hypnosis fail?'
Confession about her parents' brake-failure deaths.
